title: Section 13 CPC — When foreign judgment not conclusive

content.overview: Section 13 CPC treats a foreign judgment as conclusive on a matter directly adjudicated between the same parties, unless one of the enacted exceptions applies — want of competent jurisdiction, not on the merits, incorrect view of international law or refusal to recognise Indian law, opposed to natural justice, obtained by fraud, or founded on a breach of Indian law.
content.study: A foreign judgment is not automatically executable as an Indian decree. Section 13 is the conclusiveness filter. Section 14 raises a presumption of competence. Enforcement still needs a suit on the judgment or a reciprocal arrangement under Section 44A where that section applies. Do not skip the exception analysis.

sections.heading: Practice point
sections.body: Name the clause of Section 13 you rely on. 'It is a foreign judgment' is not a defence and not a cause of action by itself.
